question.problem:
Find the interval where the function $f(t)\times g(t)$ is differentiable, given that:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =|t-1|\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+\sqrt{1-t}\,k \\ g(t) & ={t}^{2}\,i+\sqrt{{t}^{2}-9}\,j+\operatorname{ln}⁡(3-t)\,k\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The function $F(t)=f(t)\times g(t)$ is differentiable over the common domain where both $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are differentiable. A function is differentiable if and only if each component is differentiable.

Let's now find the intervals where each of the functions $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are differentiable.

For the function $f(t):$ 

- The first component $|t-1|$ is differentiable over $(-\infty ,1)\cup (1,\infty )$, as its derivative is not defined at $t=1.$

- The second component $\operatorname{cos}⁡t$ is differentiable for all values of $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The third component $\sqrt{1-t}$ is differentiable on $(-\infty ,1)$, as its derivative is not defined at $t=1$ and the function is not defined for $t>1.$

The intersection of the domains of all three components of $f(t)$ is $(-\infty ,1).$ 

For the function $g(t):$ 

- The first component ${t}^{2}$ is differentiable for all values of $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The second component $\sqrt{{t}^{2}-9}$ is differentiable for $(-\infty ,-3)\cup (3,\infty ).$

- The third component $\operatorname{ln}⁡(3-t)$ is differentiable only on $(-\infty ,3).$

The intersection of the domains of all three components of $g(t)$ is $(-\infty ,-3).$ 

Finally, the common domain of differentiability for both functions is $(-\infty ,1)\cap (-\infty ,-3)=(-\infty ,-3).$
